title: PagerDuty Pricing 2026: Free Tier, Plans and Total Cost
summary: PagerDuty pricing is negotiated in sales calls, not published per-user rates.
body_markdown:
## Fix Noisy Paging Costs with Activepieces


To cut paging cost, keep low-urgency alerts away from PagerDuty with Activepieces, whose core is MIT-licensed. Only alerts above a severity threshold page a paid responder, and everyone else reads Slack or a ticket queue.


### Alert severity rules to cut PagerDuty seats


Start with the commercial point: every alert that reaches PagerDuty is one more reason to keep someone on a full seat.


If a monitoring tool sends everything straight in, you end up sizing the plan you buy to the noise rather than to the pages that matter.


Putting a severity gate in front changes what you're buying for.


State the rule simply: high severity goes to PagerDuty and pages a responder. Everything below the line goes somewhere else.


Write the threshold down and get the team to agree it. Then audit seats against it: anyone the rule wouldn't page is a candidate for a cheaper role or no paid seat at all.


### Routing low-urgency alerts without a page


High-severity alerts go to PagerDuty and a paged responder; low-severity alerts go through an Activepieces connector, one of 744 integrations in its open source repo, to Slack or a ticket.


Take from it that the paid path is the short one, and the volume sits on the other branch.


Activepieces sits on that second branch and prices differently from a pager seat: flows are unlimited on every plan, including free, which comes with 1,000 credits a month and up to 5 users.


Credits meter AI usage, so a flow with no AI step doesn't use them. Per-seat pricing rations automation; consumption pricing doesn't, which is why the low-urgency branch can carry the volume without adding a licence line per person.


Nobody wakes, and nothing counts against your PagerDuty usage.


Checking severity and choosing the branch can sit in that same Activepieces flow too, so the rule lives in one visible place rather than in several monitoring configs.


That also makes the trade-off plain. You're taking on a workflow to build and maintain in exchange for a smaller, better-matched PagerDuty plan.


### Why PagerDuty escalation still matters


It doesn't replace on-call scheduling, escalation policies or acknowledgement tracking. Those are what you pay PagerDuty for, and a Slack post that nobody answers doesn't escalate to a second person. If an alert is genuinely urgent, it belongs on the paged path.


So the gate has to be conservative: when you're unsure, page. A threshold set too low turns a cost saving into a missed incident, and that's the more expensive surprise.
